blocks.content:
Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution deal with citizenship.

Article 5 – Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
Article 6 – Citizenship of persons who migrated from Pakistan to India
Article 7 – Citizenship of migrants to Pakistan
Article 8 – Citizenship of persons of Indian origin residing outside India
Article 9 – Voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship
Article 10 – Continuance of citizenship
Article 11 – Power of Parliament to regulate citizenship

These articles are frequently asked directly in exams.
Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution deal with citizenship.

rows: Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution

Citizenship of persons of Indian origin residing outside India

items: Article 9 is frequently tested: Voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship automatically terminates Indian citizenship.
Article 11 grants exclusive power to Parliament (not State Legislatures) to make laws regarding citizenship.
Direct matching questions (matching Article numbers 5–11 to their exact descriptions) are very common in exams.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution deal specifically with citizenship in India.
Article 5 covers citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
Article 9 specifies that voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship leads to loss of Indian citizenship.
Article 11 gives Parliament complete authority to regulate rights of citizenship through legislation.
